newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan construction loans fall for 15th month.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan construction loans fall for 15th month.

text.p: Loans extended by Taiwan banks to construction firms fell 17.42 percent to T$392.45 billion in July from July 1995, marking the 15th consecutive month of negative growth, the central bank said on Tuesday.
July's decline followed a 17.45 percent fall in June.
In a wider picture, loans extended by Taiwan banks to all private businesses fell 2.21 percent to T$2.888 trillion in July from a year earlier, the central bank said in a statement.
July's overall decline was only the fourth monthly downtick in 10 years and all were in 1996. Lending fell 0.35 percent in January, 0.80 percent in May and 1.1 percent in June.
A central bank official attributed the flat-to-negative recent growth to an overall slowing in the economy.
Banks have been particularly cautious in granting loans to firms in the construction sector, which has seen hard times since the local real estate market peaked in 1989.
